findings.answer: The alphabet is two-layered. NATIVE layer: at each lineage step k the letter ranges over the three-element local incidence frame I_k^lambda = {x_{k-1}, xbar_{k-1}^{(lambda)}, x_k}, whose members carry the three structural roles IN, CO, NEW (IN = the parent selected by the lineage arrow, CO = the unique other parent, NEW = the composite). CANONICAL layer: after choosing one representative cyclic origin per local frame as gauge, the letters become {0,1,2}, so word labels are {0,1,2}^D. A chain (lineage) lambda = (x_0,...,x_D) with x_{k-1} in Par(x_k) does NOT have a single word; rather lambda indexes an entire depth-D word space W_D^lambda = I_1^lambda x ... x I_D^lambda — a word is a sequence choosing one frame element (one role) per step k = 1..D over the steps of that fixed lineage. The intertwiner 'maps (IN,CO,NEW) role words to LER (0,1,2) address words'. Note: in the source, lambda names the CHAIN, not the word; the word is an element w of the chain's word space W_D^lambda.
